subject: Novus MAP: token sensitivity model, evaluation plan & close timeline
messages:
From: Danielle Rivera <danielle@novushealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP kickoff + token sensitivity exercise

Alex —

Thanks for the intro call today. We have a couple of asks to nail down in the MAP before procurement will move forward: a short evaluation plan, a close timeline, and a token-cost sensitivity model that captures our expected caching behavior. We know you guys have tooling for batching/caching guidance — would be great if you could map the model to our traffic.

High level:
- POC: 2 weeks, small sample from our production traffic (privacy reviewed)
- KPI: throughput 50 RPS, p95 latency <= 350ms for LLM inferences
- Concern: our sessions have long prefixes (context up to ~4k tokens); how does prefix caching change tokens/$?

Attaching a short traffic sample and a note from the security team. Can we get a token-sensitivity workbook and a proposed MAP milestones by EOD Friday?

Thanks,
Danielle Rivera
Head of Integrations, NovusHealth
Danielle Rivera | NovusHealth

Attachments: novus_traffic_sample.json (sample), security_note.pdf (referenced)

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Rivera <danielle@novushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 13:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + token sensitivity exercise

Danielle —

Great to connect. Appreciate the traffic sample. I pulled a 48-hour extract and started a quick pass-through. Early notes below and I attached a token-sensitivity workbook (novus_map_token_model.xlsx) with two tabs: "baseline" (no caching) and "prefix-cache" (expected savings at different hit rates). Key assumptions in the workbook — please review and flag anything that doesn't match your traffic.

Quick assumptions summary (proposed):
- Avg tokens per request: 900 (sample median)
- Prefix tokens (shared per session): 1,800 on average
- Estimated prefix cache hit-rate scenarios: 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%
- Batching: continuous batching policy with 20ms accumulation window or 50 concurrent inflight requests (whichever hits first) — we’ll simulate throughput/latency tradeoffs in the workbook

What I'd like from you to finalize the MAP:
1) Confirm target pilot dates (we propose Mar 15–26 for the 2-week evaluation)
2) Provide a 7-day traffic run (json one-liner per request) or authorize the sample you sent to be used for the POC
3) Any procurement gating items (PO, standard contract redlines) so we can slot them in the timeline

We've also included a short guide (redwood-caching-batch-guide.pdf) that explains prefix cache semantics and how to interpret tokens/$ in light of batching.

I'll loop Karthik to weigh in on queuing/latency knobs; Ben and Marissa will help define the MAP milestone dates and acceptance criteria.

— Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: novus_map_token_model.xlsx, redwood-caching-batch-guide.pdf

From: Danielle Rivera <danielle@novushealth.com>

Cc: procurement@novushealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + token sensitivity exercise

Alex —

Thanks, received the workbook. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- The 1,800 prefix token number is accurate for ~60% of sessions; some diagnostic flows have prefixes ~3,500 tokens
- Procurement is asking for a worst-case tokens/$ estimate (0% cache hit) and a realistic scenario (we think 45–55% cache hit after simple session-keying)

Attached: a 7-day flattened sample (novus_traffic_sample.json) and procurement's standard SOW template. We'll target Mar 15 for start of the POC window. Can you confirm when you can deliver a final MAP (milestones, acceptance criteria, estimated pilot spend across the hit-rate scenarios)?

Best,
Danielle

Attachments: novus_traffic_sample.json

Team — forwarding Novus clarifications. They confirmed Mar 15 start. They want:
- Worst-case (0% hit), realistic (45–55%), and optimistic (75%) scenarios
- Pilot budget by scenario (tokens and dollars) and expected p95 latency for each batching configuration

Notes / ask for engineering: can we produce a quick table (single slide) that shows:
- tokens per minute at 50 RPS across the three cache-hit bands
- estimated tokens/$ assuming our standard quantized runtime (use current perf numbers)
- latency p95 impact when increasing batching window from 10ms -> 20ms -> 50ms

Also: propose a canary plan for the POC day 1: run at 5% traffic for 2 hours, measure both cache warm-up and end-to-end p95. If stable, ramp to 25% for remainder of day 1.

Ben / Karthik — can you review the workbook assumptions (I added a 'prod-sample' tab) and flag any adjustments? I captured a preliminary timeline in the draft MAP:
- Mar 8: final MAP & SOW ready
- Mar 15–26: POC window
- Mar 29: internal review and procurement signoff target

-- Alex

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Rivera <danielle@novushealth.com>, procurement@novushealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Final MAP & pilot costing — NovusHealth (attached)

Danielle / team —

Attached is the finalized MAP and the token-sensitivity workbook (novus_map_token_model.xlsx). Summary below so procurement has a one-page artifact to attach to the SOW:

MAP milestones (agreed)
- Mar 8: MAP + SOW (deliverable) — done
- Mar 15: POC starts (5% canary for 2 hours, then ramp to 25%)
- Mar 15–26: 2-week evaluation; acceptance criteria captured in workbook
- Mar 29: Procurement decision / target close

Pilot costing (summary, all numbers approximate)
- Worst-case (0% cache hit): 2-week pilot ~ 18.4M tokens -> $3,680 (assumes $0.20 per 1k tokens equivalent runtime baseline in workbook)
- Realistic (50% cache hit): 2-week pilot ~ 10.6M billed tokens -> $2,120
- Optimistic (75% hit): 2-week pilot ~ 6.8M billed tokens -> $1,360

Latency impact (p95) by batching window at 50 RPS (approx):
- 10ms window: p95 320ms
- 20ms window: p95 340ms
- 50ms window: p95 410ms (note: higher batching improves tokens/$ but pushes p95 up past their 350ms target)

Canary plan (recommended)
- Day 1: 5% traffic for 2 hrs. Verify cache warm-up (>40% prefix hits) and p95 < 350ms. If good, ramp to 25% and continue.

Next steps
1) Procurement: confirm SOW template (procurement@novushealth.com) — we'll review redlines by EOD Mar 10
2) Engineering: provide access to the 7-day traffic sample in a temp GCS bucket so we can run the POC harness (I included a one-line command in the workbook)
3) Finance: we'll issue a one-time pilot invoice after the POC start if Novus prefers to prepay the pilot spend estimate

If this looks good I’ll request the DocuSign SOW link later today and mark our internal calendar for the Mar 15 start.

— Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
